test_command: cd apps/web && npx playwright test --config tests/post-m1-phase-1-fixture-playwright.config.ts; RHYTHM_LIVE_TOKEN=$(sqlite3 "$TMPDIR/rhythm-dev-sandbox/rhythm.db" "SELECT token FROM sessions WHERE expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > datetime(*now*) ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;") npx playwright test --config tests/gateway/post-m1-phase-1-readiness-live-playwright.config.ts; cd ../electron && node --test test/post-m1-phase-1-host-policy.test.mjs test/post-m1-phase-1-packaged-host.test.mjs

criteria.text: Cold fixture launch shows one truthful readiness state, performs no live boundary request, and exposes application routes only with that applicable gate satisfied.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator executed the fixture config on 2026-08-15 (Codex cannot launch Chromium under the workspace-write sandbox). Fixture cold launch already declares readiness before exposing routes.

criteria.text: Cold live launch observes real API, engine, and auth readiness and never exposes application routes before all applicable gates succeed.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator-run against the real sandbox: 1 passed. The live config needs RHYTHM_LIVE_TOKEN, taken from the sandbox DB the same way tools/dev/sandbox.sh does: sqlite3 $TMPDIR/rhythm-dev-sandbox/rhythm.db "SELECT token FROM sessions WHERE expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > datetime(*now*) ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;". Without it the renderer never reaches Live and the criterion fails for a harness reason, not a product one.

criteria.text: Invalid requested-live/auth configuration renders one fatal readiness state and exposes neither fixture identity nor application routes.
criteria.reason: Retained M1 gateway evidence: invalid requested-live startup asserts the fatal alert and absence of the Fixture environment; no new duplicate test was written.

criteria.text: Keyboard navigation reaches every top-level destination at wide and narrow sizes with stable current-page and menuitem semantics.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator-run 8/8 twice on the Phase 1 fixture config after Unit E implemented the product change (Codex cannot launch Chromium under workspace-write). The narrow overflow loop now waits for the menu to finish taking focus before driving it; the earlier version raced the component and Enter activated the first destination instead.

criteria.text: Keyboard focus is visibly perceivable and Escape restores focus from existing menus and dialogs.
criteria.reason: Retained M1 evidence: forced-colors focus visibility and keyboard menu/dialog Escape restoration already pass in apps/web/tests/responsive-a11y.spec.ts; shell and navigation semantics are also retained in shell.spec.ts and navigation-validation.spec.ts.

criteria.text: Wide-header menu activation returns focus deterministically to its trigger.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator-run 8/8 twice on the Phase 1 fixture config after Unit E implemented the product change (Codex cannot launch Chromium under workspace-write). Shared Menu restores focus to its trigger on close. The open-focus assertion was corrected to account-profiles, the menu's actual first item; an earlier draft asserted theme-toggle and was simply wrong about the menu contents.

criteria.text: Narrow More-menu destination activation returns focus deterministically to the More trigger.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator-run 8/8 twice on the Phase 1 fixture config after Unit E implemented the product change (Codex cannot launch Chromium under workspace-write). Same shared Menu fix proves the narrow overflow case; same focus-settle wait as c2a.

criteria.text: The unsigned packaged app completes the keyboard and VoiceOver top-level navigation and focus-return check.
criteria.reason: MANUAL, assigned to AJ. Automation is not honest here: VoiceOver behaviour cannot be scripted. Procedure: launch apps/electron/dist/Rhythm.app, then with the trackpad untouched Tab through the header, confirm every top-level destination is reachable with a visible focus ring, confirm the account and More menus move focus to their first item on open and return it to the trigger on close, then enable VoiceOver (Cmd+F5) and confirm each destination announces its name and current-page state.

criteria.text: The theme setting persists through renderer reload.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator executed the fixture config on 2026-08-15 (Codex cannot launch Chromium under the workspace-write sandbox). Theme setting already persists through renderer reload.

criteria.text: An edited session setting persists through renderer reload instead of living only in component memory.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator-run 8/8 twice on the Phase 1 fixture config after Unit E implemented the product change (Codex cannot launch Chromium under workspace-write). A fixture session edit now persists across renderer reload through the existing localStorage mechanism the theme setting uses; live sessions unaffected.

criteria.text: Update failures render bounded actionable text without raw bodies, secrets, stack traces, or absolute paths.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator-corrected predicate then run: drives the ToolSurfaceState the app actually defines (unavailable) rather than an invented update-error state, and asserts a live region, a visible action, a 280-char bound, and no disclosure. Passes today.

criteria.text: Provider failures render bounded actionable text without raw bodies, secrets, stack traces, or absolute paths.
criteria.reason: Same correction as c3c against server-error. Passes today.

criteria.text: Settings persist through a full unsigned packaged host relaunch.
criteria.reason: MANUAL, assigned to AJ. Procedure: launch the packaged app, change the theme and rename a session, quit fully (Cmd+Q, not window close), relaunch, and confirm both survive. Automating this would require driving the packaged renderer UI, which the packaged smoke harness deliberately does not do.

criteria.text: The packaged host enforces the declared renderer origin, packaged-dist-only asset resolution, frozen preload allowlist, and popup/navigation/permission/download denials.
criteria.reason: Retained M1 evidence: electron-shell.test.mjs slice-5-c1..c5 and electron-unsigned-package.json slice-7-c2,c3,c5 already prove these unchanged boundaries; no GUI rerun was permitted.

criteria.text: Deep-link inputs are explicit fail-closed host-policy decisions.
criteria.reason: The host-policy unit test proves validateDeepLink accepts only rhythm://app URLs whose path passes validateRequest and rejects hostile schemes, hosts, and malformed input.

criteria.text: Native dialog inputs are explicit fail-closed host-policy decisions.
criteria.reason: The Electron host never calls dialog.*, so a dialog allowlist would guard no current surface. Re-open this criterion when the host first calls dialog.*.

criteria.text: The host acquires a single-instance lock and validates second-instance input through deep-link policy.
criteria.reason: The host-policy unit test behaviorally proves deepLinkFromArgv accepts a valid rhythm://app URL and rejects hostile or absent URLs; one narrow source assertion confirms main.mjs binds the single-instance lock plus second-instance and open-url handlers to the shared funnel.

criteria.text: Every host-owned child process is tracked and actively terminated during application shutdown.
criteria.reason: The Electron host owns no child processes today. Re-open this criterion when the host takes over spawning the local API/engine the way Flutter's ApiServerService does.

criteria.text: The unsigned packaged host enforces dialog/deep-link policy, single-instance behavior, and owned child-process shutdown at the packaged boundary.
criteria.reason: Orchestrator-run packaged evidence: two packaged launches against one shared userData contend for the lock and exactly one host runs; the yielding launch exits 0. Stable 3/3 and mutation-proved (replacing requestSingleInstanceLock() with a constant true made all three attempts report two receipts and the test fail).

note: Phase 1 RED specs use a .redspec.ts suffix so the M1 regression suite (playwright.config.ts testDir ./tests) does not collect deliberately failing contract criteria. They run only under the Phase 1 configs named in test_command. Rename them back to .spec.ts when they go green.
